img025.png.text: A probabilistic interpretation of the least-mean-square (LMS) filter. The observation model is treated as linear-Gaussian, and the posterior of the weight vector is approximated by an isotropic Gaussian distribution. The approximation is chosen by minimizing the Kullback-Leibler divergence. This gives an adaptive, step-size LMS-like algorithm whose step size is derived from the uncertainty in the estimate. The approach is a probabilistic, Bayesian view of adaptive filtering.

img065.png.text: The interlayer Berry connection polarizability (BCP) is the band-geometric origin of the crossed nonlinear dynamical Hall effect in twisted bilayers. The Hall response comes from the momentum-space curl of this quantity. It measures how the applied field shifts the interlayer Berry connection through interlayer hybridization. This produces a rectified Hall current that depends on the phase difference and magnitude of the two driving fields, so it can be used for rectification and as a transport probe of chiral symmetry in bilayers.
